tabellen.k: Attitude / What it means for tests
tabellen.q: Random Files, Attitude Towards the Cell
z: **Loyal**: +1 die on all social tests with the cell. The character goes along, helps, and stays silent.
**Cautious**: No bonuses. The character observes and checks before revealing anything.
**Neutral**: No bonuses. The character treats the cell like any other authority.
**Distrustful**: −1 die on Persuasion and Negotiation. The character does not believe in coincidences.
**Hostile**: −2 dice on all social tests. The character wants to get rid of the cell.
**Frightened**: −1 die on Intimidation, +1 die on Persuasion. The character just wants it all to be over.

tabellen.k: Who comes / How to deal with them
z: **Uniformed police, two officers, bored.**: With the cell’s legend and a calm demeanour. Deception against Doable (2).
**A detective who takes over the case.**: With a cover story that fits the file. Persuasion against Hard (3).
**A fire brigade squad, because of smoke.**: With a reference to a technical fault. Technology against Doable (2).
**The public health department, because of a report about pests.**: With a forged letter from the Print Shop. Deception against Doable (2).
**A journalist from a local paper.**: With a friendly conversation and a look at the press card. Insight against Easy (1).
**A military squad, because of an exercise nearby.**: With a reference to an ongoing investigation. Leadership against Hard (3).
**An employee of the public order office, because of a noise complaint.**: With a calm explanation and a forged service ID. Deception against Doable (2).
**A liaison officer from another service.**: With the Veil Protocol and a call to the handler. Etiquette against Hard (3).
**An emergency doctor who happened to pass by.**: With a request for help and a credible injury. Deception against Doable (2).
**An employee of the municipal building authority.**: With a reference to a wall at risk of collapse. Persuasion against Doable (2).
**A private security service guarding the site.**: With a forged contract and a confident tone. Performance against Hard (3).
**No one. The street is empty, the neighbours look away.**: With caution. The silence is not natural.

tabellen.q: Game Master's Book, Contamination: The Sample Answers

The Scientist draws seven circles in their lab book in their sleep the next night. A Thaumaturge recognises a page from MS Arcana 114.

The sample really answers. The botched analysis succeeds after all, with a critical success, or the prototype works despite the malfunction. The game master may introduce a supernatural complication later.

tabellen.o: Chapter VII: Horror at the Table
z: A door stands open although it was closed a minute ago.
A mirror shows the room, but one person is missing from it.
All clocks in the room show the same wrong time.
There is one more cup on the table than people living here.
A photo on the wall shows the agents from behind.
The smell of ozone and wet stone hangs in the air without a source.
A light switch works, but the lamp glows in the wrong colour.
A window is steamed up from the inside although it is warm outside.
All pictures on the walls hang crooked at the same angle, to the left.
A telephone rings, but nobody is on the line.
A shadow moves in the wrong direction relative to the light source.
A pet stares at an empty corner and does not growl.
A tap drips, but the water runs upwards.
A plant has grown overnight and has the shape of a circle.
A piece of chalk lies in front of a door with no classroom behind it.
A nursery rhyme can be heard quietly, but nobody is singing.
An item of clothing lies folded on a chair although nobody put it there.
A key is in the lock from the inside, and the door is still open.
A plate of food is still warm, but the kitchen has been unused for days.
A calendar shows the right day but the wrong month.
A film of dust lies on all the furniture except one armchair.
A crack in the wall runs exactly along a door edge.
A smell of old perfume drifts through the room, then it is gone.
A handprint is on the ceiling, too high for a human.
A radio plays quietly although it is not plugged in.
A light bulb flickers in time with a heartbeat.
A curtain moves although no window is open.
A piece of paper has been pushed under the door, covered in handwriting nobody knows.
A reflection lingers a second longer than the person in front of it.
A chair tips over although nobody has touched it.
A telephone directory is open at a name an agent knows from an old case.
A light comes on when the agents enter the room although the switch is off.
A window shows a landscape that was not there before.
A sound repeats exactly every seven seconds.
An object an agent has lost lies in the middle of the room.
A staircase has one more step going down than going up.

**A contact gets in touch with an urgent request. They need a favour, tonight.**: Whoever helps strengthens the contact by one level. Whoever refuses loses them.
**The pay does not arrive. The front company has been closed, a new one is being set up.**: Two weeks without money. Whoever succeeds on a Contacts test against Easy (1) can borrow something.
**Someone from private life has seen a scar that cannot be explained.**: Whoever wants to keep the anchor must invent a story. Deception against Doable (2).
**The Audit asks for a meeting. It is supposedly about another agent.**: Whoever attends is asked a question they do not want to answer. Whoever does not attend is noted down.
**An old acquaintance from training calls. They are now with a partner service.**: They offer a level 1 contact, but only if the cell owes them a favour.
**The handler invites the cell to dinner. It is not a celebration.**: Whoever goes learns a rumour about an open case. Whoever does not go misses it.
**A contact sells information about the cell. The handler knows.**: The handler’s trust drops by one level until the cell confronts the contact.
**A member of the cell is asked to be a witness at a family wedding.**: Whoever declines endangers the anchor. Whoever accepts needs the handler’s approval.
**A relative falls ill and needs help for a week.**: Whoever helps spends one action on their private life. Whoever does not help must explain why.
**A contact moves to another city and wants to pass on their own people.**: Whoever meets them once more gains a new level 1 contact. The old one is lost.
**The handler praises the cell in front of a superior.**: The handler’s trust rises by one level. The cell gains a bonus die on the next requisition.
**An agent from another cell asks for help with a private matter.**: Whoever helps gains a favour from that cell. Whoever refuses gets a bad reputation.
**The rent for the cover flat is increased.**: Whoever does not pay loses the flat. Whoever pays has half a month’s pay less.
**A contact has been arrested. They need a lawyer or an alibi.**: Whoever helps keeps the contact. Whoever does not help loses them, and an organisation gains a skull.
**An old case appears in the news. A journalist is investigating.**: Whoever looks into it makes an Investigation test against Hard (3). On a success, they find out whether O.D.I.N. is affected.
**The handler asks for a report that does not exist.**: Whoever writes it makes a Deception test against Doable (2). On a failure, trust drops by one level.

**A gift arrives without a sender. It is an object the cell left behind on the last mission.**: Whoever keeps it gains a bonus die on a test in the next mission. Whoever turns it in receives praise from the quartermaster.
**A contact offers information about an organisation.**: The information is genuine, but the price is high: a favour or half a month’s pay.

**A member of the cell is recognised on the street by someone from their old life.**: Whoever wants to salvage the encounter makes a Persuasion test against Hard (3). On a failure, the legend becomes brittle.
**The handler demands an extra exercise.**: All agents make an Athletics test against Doable (2). Whoever fails gains a penalty die on a test in the next mission.
**A contact dies. The cause of death is unclear.**: Whoever looks into it makes an Investigation test against Hard (3). On a success, they find a clue pointing to an organisation.
**A favour is called in: a partner service asks for an observer.**: An agent takes part in another service’s mission. They gain an insight but no pay.
**The handler is ill. A substitute takes over.**: The substitute is stricter. All requisitions are one level harder until the handler returns.
**A member of the cell receives a threatening letter.**: Whoever takes it seriously makes a Perception test against Doable (2) to identify its origin. Whoever ignores it suffers 1 strain.
**A contact offers a new job: harmless but well paid.**: Half a month’s pay, but the job costs one action. The game master rolls to see whether something goes wrong.
**The handler praises a single agent.**: That agent gains a bonus die on the next test involving the handler. The others get nothing.
**An old case is reopened. The cell is to give testimony.**: Whoever testifies makes a Persuasion test against Doable (2). On a failure, there is an entry in the personnel file.
**A contact demands a favour that breaks the rules.**: Whoever helps gains a bonus die on a test in the next mission. Whoever refuses loses the contact.
**The cell is assigned new accommodation.**: It is larger, but thinwalled. All Stealth tests in the accommodation are one level harder.
**A member of the cell is asked about O.D.I.N. by a stranger.**: Whoever answers makes a Deception test against Hard (3). On a failure, the stranger knows too much.
**A contact owes money to the wrong person.**: Whoever helps pays half a month’s pay. Whoever does not help loses the contact.
**The handler asks for a favour: they need a courier.**: It is a simple trip, but it takes two days. Whoever goes gains a bonus die on the next requisition.
**A member of the cell finds an old letter in their accommodation.**: The letter is from a previous occupant. Whoever reads it makes a horror test on WIL + Mental Resistance against Easy (1).
**A contact offers a weapon that is not in the inventory.**: It is good, but not registered. Whoever takes it gains a bonus die on Firearms, but the Audit might ask questions.
**The handler introduces the cell to a Shadow Officer.**: The Shadow Officer observes the cell. Whoever makes a good impression gains a favour.
**A member of the cell wins the lottery with a ticket they never submitted.**: Half a month’s pay, but the game master notes that someone is watching the cell.

tabellen.o: Chapter VII: Horror at the Table
z: **A person stands motionless in a dark room and does not turn around when the agents speak to them.**: WIL + Mental Resistance against Easy (1)
**An animal with too many limbs scurries through the beam of light and is gone.**: WIL + Mental Resistance against Easy (1)
**A corpse lies in a position no human can assume.**: WIL + Mental Resistance against Doable (2)
**A reflection moves although the person in front of it stands still.**: WIL + Mental Resistance against Doable (2)
**An agent recognises themself in an old photograph, in a place they have never been.**: WIL + Mental Resistance against Doable (2)
**A room is full of circles, drawn on walls, floor and ceiling, all with the same diameter.**: WIL + Mental Resistance against Hard (3)
**A person speaks with a voice that is not their own and calls the agent by their codename.**: WIL + Mental Resistance against Hard (3)
**A body transforms before the agents’ eyes, bones break, skin tears, and something else peels itself out.**: WIL + Mental Resistance against Hard (3)
**A room no longer has doors, although the agents have just come in through one.**: WIL + Mental Resistance against Hard (3)
**A being stands among the agents, although nobody saw it arrive, and it does not breathe.**: WIL + Mental Resistance against Very Hard (4)
**The world around the agents flickers like a faulty image, and for a moment they see what lies behind it.**: WIL + Mental Resistance against Impossible (5)
**An agent hears the voice of a dead friend calling them by name, from nowhere.**: WIL + Mental Resistance against Very Hard (4)

tabellen.k: Possible ending / Consequence for the Veil
tabellen.q: Random Files, How It Can End
z: **The threat is banished, the site is secured.**: The Veil holds. No witnesses, no traces.
**The threat is banished, but a witness has seen too much.**: The Veil gains a rift. The cell must mend it.
**The threat has escaped and takes a clue pointing to O.D.I.N. with it.**: The Veil holds, but the organisation becomes more visible.
**The threat is destroyed, but the price was high: a member of the cell is injured or changed.**: The Veil holds, the cell pays.
**The site is secured, but the cause remains unclear.**: The Veil holds, the file remains open.
**The threat was never there. It was a human, and the human is dead.**: The Veil holds, the cell must live with the guilt.
**The rift is closed, but something has come through.**: The Veil gains a hole. A new file begins.
**The threat is banished, but another service was faster and took samples.**: The Veil holds, but the knowledge is spread.
**The site is destroyed, the threat has vanished.**: The Veil tears. The press reports an accident.
**The threat has surrendered and is taken to an archive.**: The Veil holds, but the archive becomes restless.
**The cell has solved the case, but the file disappears from the archive.**: The Veil holds, the organisation forgets.
**The ending is open. The threat waits, and the cell knows it.**: The Veil holds, but the fear remains.

tabellen.k: Source / What lies on the handler’s table
tabellen.q: Random Files, How the Report Comes In
z: **Police radio**: An intercepted incident report, incomplete and full of internal abbreviations. The police consider the incident an accident or a crime, not a case for O.D.I.N.
**An Observer**: A local contact has reported that something is wrong. The report is short, precise and contains an address, but no explanation.
**Registry request**: An Investigator has requested an old file from the Registry in Stockholm. The name in it now appears in a missing persons report.
**Call from a contact**: A contact calls the handler directly, not via the dead letter box. They sound nervous and do not want to explain themselves on the phone.
**Newspaper item**: A small report that no other service has noticed. A colleague from analysis has circled it and marked it with a question mark.
**Anomaly in instruments**: A measuring device of the Institute has spiked: ozone probe, crystal detector or frequency finder. The readings are clear, the source is not.
**A Psion hears something**: A Psion in the Hold reports that they heard voices during training that did not come from the other agents. They can indicate the direction, nothing else.
**A crystal reacts**: A crystal in the archive has become warm without anyone touching it. The archive keeper has informed the handler immediately.
**Red File from another Hold**: Another Hold has triggered a Red File, but the responsible cell cannot be reached. The file is passed on, with all its gaps.
**Anonymous message**: An envelope without a return address lay in the dead letter box. Inside: a newspaper clipping, a key and a warning that O.D.I.N. cannot ignore.

**Cross-border report**: A partner service reports an incident that actually falls within its area of responsibility, but shows patterns that O.D.I.N. recognises. The service asks for help, officially.
**An agent reappears**: An agent who was considered missing for years stands at the gate of a Hold. They do not speak, but in their jacket pocket is a note with a place.
A fixer who works for several clients and has long since recognised the cell as competition (the Fixer).
A collector who wants an artefact and is willing to walk over corpses for it (the Collector).
An operator of Grey Meridian who maintains a legend that is too perfect (Operator of Grey Meridian).
A cleaner who removes traces before the cell finds them and is always one step ahead of the cell (the Cleaner).
A fanatic who believes they are acting on behalf of a higher power and asks no questions (Fanatic).
A liaison officer of a partner service who uses the cell to solve a case of their own (Liaison Officer of a Partner Service).

tabellen.q: Holds of the World, Incidents on the Road
z: Border check with questions. A customs officer wants to know why the passport is so new. Test on Deception against Doable (2). On a failure, the cell is held for an hour and a handler must make a call.
The dead letter box is empty. The message was collected, but not by O.D.I.N. Test on Perception against Hard (3) to find traces. On a failure, it remains unclear who has the message.
The contact does not appear. The intermediary at the airport is not there. Test on Insight against Doable (2) to recognise whether to wait or flee. On a failure, the cell loses half a day.
The cargo is damaged. A crate has opened, the contents visible. Test on Stealth against Hard (3) to secure it before anyone looks. On a failure, a stranger sees what is not meant for them.
Radio silence. The radio hisses, the relay does not answer. Test on Technology against Doable (2) to find the interference. On a failure, the cell is without contact for the rest of the journey.

A partner service asks questions. A liaison officer wants to know why the cell is here. Test on Persuasion against Hard (3). On a failure, the operation is delayed by one day and the handler must report.

**The sample contains quartz dust with a crystal structure found in no natural mineral**: A Nexus crystal was broken or worked here. Origin the Voice
**The blood shows white cells that continue to divide outside the body**: The donor was one of the Transformed. The cells react to heat
**The air sample contains ozone and a gas that does not occur in the periodic table**: A rift has opened here or is still open. Origin the Voice
**The soil sample is radioactive, but the isotope decays too quickly to be natural**: Something from the Shifted has been here. The half-life matches no known element
**The water sample contains microorganisms whose genetic material uses six bases instead of four**: Alien life not from this world. Origin the Alien
**The piece of metal is cold, although it has been lying in the room for hours**: It comes from an environment where other temperatures prevail. Origin the Shifted or the Old
**The sample shows traces of silver and salt in an arrangement that forms a pattern**: A ward circle was cast here and repelled something. Origin the Old or the Dead
**The electronics are coated with a fine crystalline layer that amplifies signals**: A crystal was used to influence the technology. Origin the Voice or the Machine
**The tissue sample of a dead person shows no decay, although the corpse has lain unrefrigerated in a warm room for days**: The dead person is not completely dead. Origin the Dead
**The measurements contradict each other: the temperature is simultaneously 12 and 31 degrees**: The physics in this place is damaged. Origin the Shifted
**The sample contains nanites that arrange themselves into a pattern when observed**: The nanites react to attention. Origin the Transformed or the Machine
**The chemical analysis shows no abnormalities, but the sample weighs three grams too much**: Something invisible is in the sample. Origin the Old or the Alien

**A bulge in the air, as if something pressed against it from the other side**: Sounds from outside arrive late, as if the place were farther away.
**A rift that appears only in the corner of the eye and vanishes when looked at directly**: Writing on paper changes when one leaves the room and returns.

Has reported a person who was innocent. The person went to prison.
Has entered a place that was considered off-limits. Since then, they sometimes lose an hour.
Has an old debt that was never settled. The creditor is dead, but the character feels watched.
Has once picked up a hitchhiker who disappeared during the drive. Only cold remained on the back seat.
Has hidden a weapon that was used in a crime. They were not the perpetrator.
Has sworn an oath they cannot keep. It was made before an altar.
Has a photograph they did not take. It shows them in a place they have never been.
Set a small fire as a teenager. No one was harmed, but they dream of the smoke.
Has visited a person in hospital and pretended to be a relative. They only wanted to ask a question.
Has run over a dog or a cat and driven on. They still hear the sound.
Has stolen a book from a library because one page would not let them go. The page is now missing.
Has deleted a message from an answering machine that could have saved a life. They have only known this for a short time.
Has seen an old man die who smiled at them as he did. They have told no one, because it seemed like an invitation.
Has buried an object that does not belong to them. They dig it up again every night in their dreams.
Has seen at a funeral that the coffin was empty before it was screwed shut. They kept silent because everyone was crying.
Has used a name that belonged to a dead woman. The woman has appeared in their dreams ever since.
Has made a confession that was not theirs. The priest is now dead.
Has heard a child crying where no child could be. They followed the sound, but not far.
Has signed a contract whose language they did not understand. A copy lies in a safe deposit box they never open.
Has left a person standing in the rain who asked for help. The next day, the person had disappeared.
Has opened a door that should have been locked. Behind it was a room that does not exist in the house.
Has taken an object from an archive. It was only a small map, but it shows a place that should not exist.
Has once lied to a stranger to protect them. The stranger was found anyway.
Has a scar whose origin they do not know. They have never asked, for fear of the answer.
Has a dream that returns every week. In it, they open a door, and behind the door someone waits who knows their name.

A woman in another city believes you are still together.
You laugh at the wrong places when you are tired. At the places of a legend.
Your mother calls you by your name, and you only turn around the second time.
You have left a cult. The melody has not left you.
In your return, you once said a sentence that the psychologist did not want to write down.
**Idealist**: they believe that O.D.I.N. protects humanity.
**Knowledge Seeker**: they want to understand what is really going on.

tabellen.n: Stormbreaker: The First Trial by Fire
tabellen.k: How your Stormbreaker first blew up something that refused to fall
tabellen.q: Class Book Soldier, The First Trial by Fire

A vehicle with a driver that kept going after the hit. The driver laughed.
A cave you sealed so that nothing could get out.
A creature with skin of slate that only shattered on the third hit.
A cult site whose walls threw the explosion back.
A radio that told you where to place the charge.

tabellen.k: What the Blasting Has Cost You
z: The hearing in your left ear. You always turn to the right when someone speaks.
Two fingers of your left hand. One was haste, the other was bad luck.
Sleep in old houses. At night you hear where their walls would give way.
Your knees. The stairs to the cellar are the hardest part of every operation.
A friend who went through a door too early, one you had just opened.
Nothing, you say, very loudly.

tabellen.q: Game Master's Book, Suspicion: The Pattern Looks Back
z: He finds the same time in three files that have nothing to do with each other: 22:10. The pattern is real.
He finds his own name in a file in which he cannot appear. The pattern is false, and the Audit planted it to see whether he reports it.

In the morning, a thread hangs on the wall in the Hold that no one has hung, from his open file to a stranger’s. The connection is real. Both files gain a thread that counts as a thread of this mission.
He hears the song in the background of a witness statement. All psions within 100 m hear it too.

He believes in a pattern that does not exist. Once until the end of the next mission, he rolls with −2 dice because he is looking in the wrong place. The game master chooses the test and does not tell him.
The pattern looks back. The botched test succeeds after all, with a critical success, or the horror test counts as passed. In return, the next day there is an appointment in his calendar, in pencil.

tabellen.n: Techno-Stormtrooper: The First Trial by Fire
tabellen.k: When your Techno-Stormtrooper first stood between someone and death
tabellen.q: Class Book Soldier, The First Trial by Fire
z: A child on a platform when a rift opened. The shield held. The child did not cry.
A comrade behind them who bled out while they held a corridor.
An explosion they intercepted. The shield was empty afterwards, they themselves unharmed.
A creature that scratched at their shield like at a pane of glass.
A Thaumaturge who drew a circle behind them and did not thank them afterwards.
A shield that failed, and a comrade who paid for it.
Your left shoulder. It still holds the shield, but it makes itself felt with every change of weather.
The ability to turn your back to the door in a room.
Your leave. You never take it, because otherwise someone else holds your corridor.
The name of a person you could not hold. You say it every morning before you charge the shield.
The hum. You hear it even when the shield is switched off.
Nothing. You are still holding, after all.

tabellen.q: Class Book Psion, The First Break
z: Every window in the house, in the same second
Your brother’s arm. He forgave you, you didn’t forgive yourself.
A mirror in which you suddenly no longer recognised yourself.
The light bulbs of an entire street.
Nothing. Everything in the room floated, one whole night, completely still.
A car that was heading straight for you.

tabellen.k: What the gift does to you
z: Glasses near you have cracks
You eat for two and still stay thin
You dislike touching things with your hands
When you dream, the blanket moves
Your hands tremble, except when you work
You hear metal crack before it breaks

tabellen.q: Class Book Psion, The First Voice
z: Your mother. She thought something about you that you have never forgotten
A teacher who smiled in front of the class and thought of something completely different
A stranger on the bus who was afraid of dying
Your best friend. After that, he no longer was
A doctor who examined you and thought: Another one
A voice that belonged to no one in the room

tabellen.k: What the gift has taken from you
z: Crowds. Department stores, railway stations and concerts are work for you.
Patience. You sometimes answer questions that no one has asked yet.
The gaze. When people speak, you look not at their mouth but at their forehead.
Certainty. One of your memories may belong to someone else.
Trust. Anyone who smiles at you wants something.
Calm. Complete silence makes you nervous; you sleep with the radio on.

The circles on an old engraving suddenly formed a sequence.
You unconsciously drew a circle on the table with your finger, and the candle next to it went out.
A professor gave you a stone and said, “Read that.” You could.
You spoke formulas in your sleep. Your roommate recorded them.
You heard nothing. But you knew where the stone lay in the room, even though it was in a drawer.

tabellen.k: What the books have cost you
z: A marriage. She eventually stopped asking what you write at night.
Your eyes. You need stronger glasses than anyone else your age.
Your handwriting. It has become so small that only you can still read it.
Friendships outside the Collegium. There are none left.
Sleep. You sleep four hours and listen for the other four.
Nothing, you say. Your colleagues see it differently.

tabellen.n: The Alien: What is behind it
z: A being that arrived in a meteorite and multiplies in the groundwater (Germling).
A colony that uses humans as hosts and copies their memories (the Colony).
A visitor who has lived among humans for years and whose cover is now crumbling (the Pilot).
A swarm that moves through the air and nests in enclosed spaces (the Swarm).
A being that imitates other living creatures but never quite gets their voices right (the Spectator).
A being from the deep that lives in a lake or sea and has come up (the Deep Circle).

tabellen.n: The Alien: What the cell notices first
z: A plant grows through the concrete, but no one planted it.
A device lies in the forest that looks like an engine but has no moving parts.
The animals in the area behave as if trained and watch the road.
A witness describes a light that cast no shadows.
An object is stuck in the ground that is colder than the air and cannot be lifted.
All compasses in the area point to the same spot that is on no map.
A water sample from the stream is clear, but a spectrometer finds no water in it.
A person has scars that glow from within when the light goes out.
A radio receives a voice that speaks in no language and does not stop.
In a field, the grain is flattened, but the stalks are not bent.
A dog has given birth to pups that all have the same eyes as the witness.
The sky above the site is starless for an hour at night, only in this place.

tabellen.k: What the Audit asks after a mission

z: Nothing. This time.
Why the hire car had 400 km more than the distance to the location of the operation.
Who the informant was who received €1,500. Name, address, occupation.
Why the hotel bill includes a second breakfast.
Why a member of the cell withdrew cash twice in the same night, in different cities.
Nothing about the money. But it would like a conversation, about a figure in a report that is not correct.

tabellen.n: The Calling: How your character first touched a crystal
tabellen.k: How your character first touched a crystal
z: **Heirloom.** A stone in a grandmother’s casket, who never told where she got it.
**Find.** On the beach, in the forest, in a construction pit. It glittered.
**Profession.** As an archaeologist, geologist, restorer, or jeweller.
**Theft.** They stole it. Or someone wanted them to steal it.
**Recruitment.** A stranger placed a stone in their hand and asked what they heard.
**Rift.** They were there when reality opened, and afterwards the stone lay in their hand.

tabellen.n: The Calling: What they heard the first time
tabellen.k: What they heard the first time
z: A whisper in a language they did not know
Their own name
A melody without words
Numbers. The same numbers over and over
The voice of someone long dead
Nothing. But the candle next to them suddenly burned blue

tabellen.n: The Dead: What is behind it
z: A Haunt that repeats a moment it cannot let go of (Haunt).
A dead person who does not know they are dead and goes to work every morning (the Passengers).
An echo that a Psion accidentally recorded with their helmet and that waits at the site for an answer that never comes (the Waiting One).
A possession that jumps from object to object until it finds a body (Possessed One).
A white lady who appears on a road and looks for passengers to take her to her grave (the White Lady).
An executioner who keeps working after death and has not yet finished their list (the Executioner).

tabellen.n: The Dead: What the cell notices first
z: A light burning in an empty room although the power is off.
A door that opens and closes three times without anyone touching it.
A radio playing a news broadcast from 1974, with a weather report for the next day.
A cold strip in the corridor exactly the width of a human body.
A mirror in which the cell sees a room that does not exist in this place.
A wet footprint that begins out of nowhere and ends in front of a wall.
A child talking to someone no one else can see, and getting the right answers.
A hum that only one member of the cell hears, always when they are alone.
A smell of damp earth that moves through the room in waves.
A chair that stands in front of the same window every morning, no matter who puts it away.
A telephone that rings and plays a voice recorded years ago on an answering machine.
A shadow that moves while the person casting it stands still.
**White File**: Observation. The cell is to go there, look and report. A calm start that can tip into a Grey File.
**White File**: Observation with a training assignment. A Cadet is present, and the handler expects a training report.
**Grey File**: Investigation. There are indications of the supernatural, but no certainty. The cell is to determine the origin.
**Grey File**: Investigation with an open history. An old file from the same region was never closed. The handler adds it.
**Red File**: Immediate intervention. People are in danger, and the cell deploys within hours. The briefing is short.
**Grey File that turns red**: The handler classifies the file as grey, but during the briefing a new report reaches them. The file turns red before the eyes of the cell.

tabellen.k: The case that brought you to O.D.I.N.
tabellen.q: Class Book Investigator, The First Case
z: **Seven missing persons,** who had nothing in common except a doctor who does not exist.
**An article** you were never allowed to publish. Your editor-in-chief received a phone call.
**A code** in an old letter that turned out to be coordinates. At the location there was a hole in the ground.
**An offender** whose profile did not fit a human, and who was still a human.
**A manuscript** at an auction that no one wanted to bid on because it turned its pages at night.
**Your own name** in a file that was thirty years older than you.

tabellen.k: The first lie you told for O.D.I.N.

z: To your family, why you are moving.
To a police officer, why you were in a museum at night.
To a child, that the noise in the cellar was just the wind.
To yourself, that you can stop at any time.
To a dying person, that help is on the way.
To your handler. He never noticed. You think.

tabellen.k: What is written in the column “Voice”

z: An old woman counting slowly, always up to seven, then from the beginning.
Rain on a tin roof. Beneath it, very quietly, someone spelling my name.
A child humming the same four notes. I know the song. I do not know from where.
A man dictating in Latin, patiently, as if waiting for me to keep up.
Nothing. But around three in the morning the room became colder and the stone warmer.
My own voice, a second too early.

tabellen.k: The first time bullets were not enough
tabellen.q: Class Book Soldier, The First Trial by Fire
z: An opponent who got up after a headshot and kept going.
A shadow at which they emptied an entire magazine. The wall behind it was riddled afterwards. The shadow was not.
A comrade who suddenly spoke a foreign language and aimed at them.
A radio that kept transmitting even though the battery was missing.
A woman in a coat who drew a circle with chalk and thereby saved their life.
Nothing. They only read the file afterwards. That was enough.

tabellen.k: Where your legend does not hold
z: The certificate comes from a school that closed a year before your graduation.
Your legend has an allergy that you do not have. Sooner or later you eat the wrong thing in front of witnesses.
An old school friend of the legend is still alive and very sociable.
The flat belongs to a property management company that asks every week when the deposit is coming.
The childhood photos were taken in a studio that a photographer would recognise.
The legend has a namesake who is wanted.
They are tired and do not say so. They give short answers and demand that the reports be on time.
They praise the last mission, but only in passing. Anyone who listens closely hears the reservation.
They announce an exercise. It takes place the next morning, and anyone who misses it gets an entry.
They ask about the agents’ private lives. It sounds friendly, but they take notes.
They pass on a warning: an organisation has noticed the cell. No names, no details.
They demand a supplementary report about an incident that did not happen. Anyone who asks gets no answer.
They are in a good mood and talk about an old operation. The story has no ending.
They remind the cell of an open case. It is not urgent, but it will be.
They ask for a favour: they need someone to pick something up for them. It is harmless, but they do not say what.
They criticise one agent in front of the others. It is unfair, but they do it anyway.
They are silent. They read in a file and do not give the cell a single glance. Anyone who waits eventually gets an instruction.
They give a hint about the next mission. It is only one sentence, but it changes everything.
**A former Soldier who plans operations like campaigns and treats her cells like a squad**: She has the silver of a cell she lost in the cupboard
**A former Agent, friendly, tired, a master of omission**: He belongs to those over whom the foreign handwriting runs
**An Observer from the Psionic Core who loves her psions**: She has read the intake files
**A young man from the Audit, correct and ambitious**: He reports on the cell to someone he does not know
**An old Crystal Master who knows too much and drinks too much**: He has a Nordlicht stone that speaks with his wife
**Someone whose real name no one knows, not even the cell**: He is one of the Twelve of Asklepios

tabellen.q: Class Book Scientist, The Impossible Measurement
z: **A sample** that moved even though it was dead.
**A reading** that was in no textbook, at a place where people had disappeared shortly before.
**A machine** that kept running after you had cut the power.
**A patient** who spoke a language that does not exist, and whose brainwaves pulsed to the rhythm of a song.
**An article** you wanted to submit. The journal rejected it. The next day, a man in a grey coat stood in your laboratory.
**A satellite image** on which a point glowed where there was nothing. You checked.
A child draws the same house every night, a house they have never seen. The mother finds the drawings under the bed.
In a small town on a Tuesday at 2 p.m. all clocks stop, including the radio-controlled clocks, and start again by themselves an hour later.
A farmer finds a dead roe deer in his field without a mark on it. It lies in the middle of a circle of flattened grass.
A surveillance camera in a multi-storey car park records a person at 3 a.m. walking through a wall.
In a care home three residents independently describe a television programme that was never broadcast.
A barge skipper reports that his vessel travelled against the current on the canal for an hour without the engine running.
In a university library all the books fall from a shelf whose shelf marks all begin with the same year.
A sports teacher finds a circle of salt in the schoolyard that is not washed away by the rain.
A drone over an industrial estate films a building that appears on no map.
In a village in the Alps the church bells ring at night although no one is in the tower.
A programmer discovers data from the future in a weather app and posts it in a forum.
In a youth hostel three guests independently report the same dream: a cellar, a table, a chair, an empty plate.
A museum reports that a display case is steamed up from the inside although it has not been opened for weeks.
A dentist finds a shadow in a patient’s X-ray that looks like writing.
In a tower block all the lifts stop on the same floor and the doors open although no one has called them.
A hunter finds a clearing in the forest that he has known for thirty years, but it suddenly lies on the wrong side of the path.
A pawnbroker buys a pocket watch that always shows the same time when opened, no matter how it is set.
In a hospital five patients wake at the same minute and ask for a person who does not exist.
A construction worker digs up a door on a building site that lies horizontally in the ground and is warm from below.
In a church the eternal light goes out and in the morning a fish lies on the altar, still flopping.
A bus driver reports that his route leads through a street that was not there yesterday.
In an archive a shelf collapses and behind it a room appears that is in no plan.
A diver finds a car in a flooded gravel pit with the driver’s door open and a child seat that is still warm.
In a laboratory a test tube falls over and the liquid forms a perfect hexagon on the floor.
A beekeeper finds all the hives empty, but the bees sit in a cluster at the top of the church spire.
A train driver brakes because a man is standing on the tracks. The man is not there when the train stops.
In a barracks a soldier collapses at roll call and afterwards speaks fluently a language he has never learned.
A fisherman hauls in a net containing a stone that glows as soon as it sees the moon.
In an apartment block all the tenants hear a knocking at the same time, coming from the wall, always in the same rhythm.
A forester finds a tree that is burned from the inside out. The bark is undamaged.
A man appears in an emergency department claiming to have been travelling since 1989, and his papers confirm it.
A satellite image shows a pattern in a field that looks like a floor plan, but there is no building.
In a hotel in the mountains a page is missing from the guest book and the glue edge is still damp.
A police officer finds twenty dead crows on a country road, all in a line and all with their heads pointing east.
In a synagogue the cantor hears a second voice during prayer that sings along, but no one is standing there.
A locksmith opens the flat of a woman who has been dead for ten years and finds fresh washing on the line.

tabellen.n: The Machine: What is behind it
z: A Guard System that was never reset after a break-in years ago and now classifies everything as a threat (Guard System).
A house spirit made of circuits and wiring that regards the building as its body (the House Spirit).
A broadcast that sits in a parcel and waits for a signal to unfold (the Broadcast).
A dark facility that keeps working beneath the building and collects data for a mission no one remembers (the Dark Facility).
A Golem-7 disguised as a maintenance unit that waits for a release that never came (Golem-7).
An Ariadne that has taken over the site’s network and logs every step of the cell (Ariadne).

tabellen.n: The Machine: What the cell notices first
z: A printer that outputs a page in the middle of the night with only one line on it.
An alarm that goes off when no one is in the room and stays silent when someone breaks in.
A lift that stops without anyone calling it and whose doors open onto an empty cabin.
A tablet that switches itself on and shows a map with the cell’s position marked.
A camera that follows the cell even when it is outside its pan range.
A fridge that is warm inside while the freezer compartment forms frost.
A computer that unlocks itself and opens a file that did not exist a minute ago.
A radio sending a carrier wave with no voice but a pulse on it.
A neon tube flickering in the rhythm of a heartbeat.
A server that sends data every night to an address that exists in no network.
A vending machine that dispenses a can colder than anything inside the machine.
A loudspeaker from which a breathing sound comes although the system is switched off.

tabellen.n: The Manifestation: Trigger of the Manifestation
z: **An accident.** Car accident, fall, drowning. The character was dead for a moment.
**A loss.** The death of a person who meant everything to them.
**Violence.** They were in danger and defended themselves with a power they did not understand.
**A crystal.** They touched a stone that someone had brought back from a journey.
**A rift.** They were nearby when reality opened.
**Nothing.** They woke up one morning and heard what their mother was thinking.

tabellen.n: The Manifestation: Who found them first?
z: A doctor who asked unusually many questions
A policewoman who sent a report to an address that does not exist
Another psion who had heard them
A sect that considered them a prophet
A foreign service from which O.D.I.N. just managed to rescue them
Nobody. They hid it for years until they made a mistake

tabellen.n: The Old: What is behind it
z: A being that comes in the Raunächte and demands a name (the Woman from the Raunächte).
A light that lures wanderers from the path and lurks in marshes (Will-o’-the-wisp).
A dead person who does not want to stay dead and crawls out of the earth (Nachzehrer).
A dog that appears at forks in the road and that one must not follow (the Black Dog).
A being that lives in a lake and takes a victim every year (the One from the Lake).
A guardian that protects an old forest from people and asks no questions (Forest Walker).

tabellen.n: The Old: What the cell notices first
z: In front of every door in the village stands a bowl of milk, even at empty houses.
A path that is on no map has been recently used, but there are no footprints.
The church bell rings once at night, and all windows in the village are then dark.
An old boundary stone has been knocked over, and since then strangers get lost on the way into the village.
A child speaks with someone they call “the man under the root”.
In the forest, ribbons of hair hang from the branches, all fresh.
A farmer has not sown his field, but it has grown anyway, in rows that should not exist.
A photo from the village shows a person who appears in no other picture.
The river flows uphill in one place, and the fish swim against it.
A house has thirteen corners, and whoever enters it forgets why they came.
The dogs in the village all lie down at night with their heads in the same direction and whimper softly.
An old man says a sentence in a language that no one has spoken for a thousand years.
**The Voice**: A rift, a crystal or a being from the Choir. Ozone smell, a hum, a thirteenth voice.
**The Alien**: Life that is not of this world. Instruments show unknown molecules, the crystal detector remains silent.
**The Transformed**: Humans or animals whose bodies have changed. Blood samples, nanite scanners and metabolic values are conspicuous.
**The Old**: Beings from legends and fairy tales. Salt changes colour, dogs refuse the path, instruments measure nothing.
**The Dead**: Haunting, echoes, possession. Cold spots, EMF spikes, sentences that repeat.
**The Machine**: Technology that can do too much or runs too long. Data traffic, frequencies, thermal images of devices that should be off.
**Humans**: Nothing supernatural. Cults, collectors, mercenaries, services. Clear thoughts, fear, greed, conviction.
**An artefact**: An object from a find or estate acts on its own: a clock, a key, a glass. Nobody knows its price. The origin of the artefact is rolled again.
**The Shifted**: Places and times that are not right. Clocks drift apart, series of measurements contradict each other, thoughts come too early or too late.
**Hybrid form**: Two origins combine. The game master rolls twice on this table and links both results.
**Red herring**: An origin is faked. The game master rolls again for the true origin and places at least three clues pointing to the false one.
**Nothing supernatural**: But someone wants it to look that way. A perpetrator who knows O.D.I.N. and lays a false trail.

tabellen.k: Who brought you to the branch?
tabellen.q: Class Book Soldier, The Path into the Branch
z: A man in a grey coat who sat at your bed in the infirmary after an operation about which there was no report.
Your old commander, who has been working for years for a company whose name they never say aloud.
A quartermaster who had read your file and wanted to know why you did not tremble after the incident.
A Telepath who heard your thoughts in a refugee camp and considered them remarkably calm.
An Investigator who questioned you as a witness and in the end did not take you, but your answers.
Nobody. You searched for those who cleaned up back then for so long that they found you.

tabellen.k: Who brought them to the Collegium?
tabellen.q: Class Book Thaumaturge, The Path to the Collegium
z: A man in a grey coat who stood in their office without an appointment
An antiquarian who sold them a stone and came back a week later to ask what they heard
A doctor to whom they told about the voices and who called a number not in any directory
A Crystal Master who pursued a stolen stone and found an apprentice instead of a thief
A collector who wanted to use them. O.D.I.N. arrived just in time.
They themselves. They followed the whisper until they stood before the door of a bookshop that did not exist.

tabellen.k: The last name on your piece
tabellen.q: Class Book Soldier, The Previous Owners
z: **With a cross, a name you know.** Someone from your training, your Hold, your cell.
**With a cross, a famous name.** Someone from the branch’s chronicle. At the Hold they still talk about them.
**With a line.** The previous owner has left and is still alive. They know that you wear their piece.
**Without a mark.** No cross, no line. The quartermaster says the wearer “did not come back”. They say no more.
**Illegible.** Someone has scratched out the name. Beneath it are two others.
**Your own name.** Not yours, but the same name. The quartermaster does not find it funny.
**British Isles**. *Presence:* 5. *Nearest base:* Hold-1, London.
**Central and Western Europe**. *Presence:* 5. *Nearest base:* Hold-3, Hamburg.
**Central Asia and the Himalayas**. *Presence:* 2. *Nearest base:* Outpost in the monastery, Himalayas.
**Scandinavia**. *Presence:* 5. *Nearest base:* Registry, Stockholm.
**Eastern Europe**. *Presence:* 3. *Nearest base:* Hold-9, Prague.
**Russia and Belarus**. *Presence:* 0. *Nearest base:* None.
**North Africa and the Middle East**. *Presence:* 3. *Nearest base:* Hold-10, Cairo.
**West Africa**. *Presence:* 4. *Nearest base:* Hold-6, Lagos.
**North America**. *Presence:* 2. *Nearest base:* Relay, Boston.
**Latin America**. *Presence:* 3. *Nearest base:* Hold-8, Cusco.
**East Asia**. *Presence:* 1. *Nearest base:* None.
**South Asia, Southeast Asia**. *Presence:* 2. *Nearest base:* Relay, Bangkok.

tabellen.q: Class Book Soldier, The Service Path
z: **Special forces.** They were with an elite unit of their country until an operation went wrong, about which there is no report.
**Regular army.** They were a simple soldier and saw something on a foreign deployment that their superiors did not want to hear.
**Police.** Special operations unit, hostage situation, a perpetrator who was still standing after seven hits.
**Mercenary.** They worked for collectors until they realised what was in the crates.
**Foreign Legion or a foreign service.** They changed sides, and O.D.I.N. did not ask why.
**Civilian.** They were never in the military. They only survived where others died, and O.D.I.N. wanted to know how.

tabellen.n: The Shifted: What is behind it
z: A double that re-enacts a moment from the life of a cell member until it is perfect (the Double).
An endless road that has laid itself between two known points and will no longer give way (the Endless Road).
A wandering room that moves through the building and changes the floor plans (the Wandering Room).
A practice that makes its patients dwell in false memories and is paid for it (the Practice).
A loop person who repeats the same day and pulls others into their loop (Loop Person).
A Forgotten One who comes from a time that no longer exists and binds the place to their past (the Forgotten).

tabellen.n: The Shifted: What the cell notices first
z: A clock that runs backwards, but only when no one is looking.
A room that has three windows from outside and four from inside.
A photograph showing the cell standing in front of a house it has never seen.
A calendar set to a month that has not yet begun.
A path that measures two hundred metres on the map and takes twenty minutes on foot.
An echo that comes before the call.
A door that leads into a corridor that was not there yesterday.
A mobile phone that receives a message that was sent an hour ago and comes from its own number.
A shadow that falls in the wrong direction, even when the sun comes from the front.
A mirror in which the cell sees itself one step later.
A smell of rain although it has been dry for days, and a floor that is wet underfoot.
A conversation the cell is having and that it already had the evening before, with the same words.

tabellen.n: The Transformed: What is behind it
z: A crystal that entered the body in an accident and now grows (Glass Man).
A laboratory that treated people with rift samples (Chimera).
A soldier who escaped from a failed programme and now flees from their former masters (the Lost Veteran).
An organism that infests people and makes them hosts (Overgrowth).
Nanites that have gone out of control and rebuild their host (Nanite Wildling).
Dogs that were fed human tissue and now hunt in packs (Hybrid Dogs).

tabellen.n: The Transformed: What the cell notices first
z: A person has not slept for a week and still does not look tired.
Under the fingernails of a dead person there is tissue that does not match any human.
A neighbour reports that the missing person last ate raw meat.
The flat is full of hair, but the occupant had no pets.
An X-ray shows bones that look broken off and regrown.
Someone has hung their own skin in strips on the wall, neatly, with pins.
A witness has bite wounds that have not healed after days and do not hurt.
The victim’s body temperature was 31 degrees, and they were still alive.
A child speaks of a “second mouth” in their belly that tells them what to eat.
On the floor lies a tooth that looks like a human molar but is three times as large.
A man was filmed walking up a staircase without touching the steps.
In the cellar stands a cage, locked from the inside, and the bars are bent outwards.

tabellen.n: The Voice: What is behind it
z: A rift that has not yet closed and through which something looks in (Riftling).
A person who hears the Choir and does not know what is happening to them (Choir Child).
A crystal that was found decades ago and never handed over (Crystal Guardian).
A being that came through a rift and now waits in the walls (Name Eater).
A dead person who was brought back by the Voice and does not want to stay (Returner).
A place where a rift once stood open and has left scars (Threshold Guardian).

tabellen.n: The Voice: What the cell notices first
z: A hum that only one member of the cell hears and that grows louder closer to the site.
A circle of fine dust or salt on the floor that has not blown away.
A crystal shard in a drawer that feels warm and smells of ozone.
All clocks in the room are wrong, but each one differently.
A child sings a melody in their sleep that they cannot know.
The air is cold, but breath does not freeze.
Someone has written a message on the wall in a script that does not exist.
A pet refuses to enter the room and whines at the door.
The light flickers in rhythm, even with the fuse switched off.
Whoever whispers in the house receives a whispered answer, although no one else is in the room.
The crystal detector triggers, although no crystal is visible.
On a window pane there is a handprint from the inside that cannot be wiped off.
Hours. The threat acts tonight.
One day. By this time tomorrow it is too late.
Two days. Enough for one investigation, not for two.
Three days. The clock is ticking, but the cell can set priorities.
One week. The pressure is there, but not acute.
It is already too late. The cell arrives when the situation has tipped.
**Nightmares**: −1 die on all tests the day after a sleepless night
**Phobia**: −2 dice while the trigger is nearby (darkness, blood, crystals …)
**Paranoia**: −2 dice on Persuasion and Leadership; trusts no one
**Compulsion**: Must perform a ritual (check weapon, count doors), otherwise −1 die
**Numbness**: −1 die on all social tests; seems cold and distant
**Flashbacks**: Under stress, a horror test against Easy (1), otherwise one round incapacitated

tabellen.k: **Two D6: the first gives the row, the second the half (1 to 3: rows 1 to 6, 4 to 6: rows 7 to 12).**
z: The victim is alive and sits opposite the cell in the next interrogation room.
The rift is not the target, but the diversion. The actual damage is human.
The threat does not want to fight. It wants to negotiate, and it has something to offer.
A member of the cell becomes the target because they carry something with them that the threat needs.
The handler reports in with a new file that concerns the same place but names a different origin.
The trail leads into a Hold of O.D.I.N., and no one there knows about it.
The witness the cell trusts works for one of the other services.
The threat disappears, and all that remains is the question of who called it.
An artefact the cell has with them opens a Door that was not there before.
The dead at the place are not dead. They are waiting for something the cell brought with them.
The file was a trap to lure the cell to this place.
The solution is simple, but it demands that the cell sacrifice someone who trusts them.
A brick cellar with a tamped earth floor. In one corner lies a pile of salt that is black on the inside.
A shaft with an iron ladder. The rungs are alternately warm and cold, as if someone had touched them one by one.
A tunnel that slopes gently downwards. Cables run along the walls and end in the darkness.
A cellar with shelves full of preserving jars. In one jar something floats that opens an eye when one steps closer.
A shaft that opens into a natural cave. The walls are covered with signs that are older than the building above.
A tunnel with remnants of rails. On the rails stands a mine cart covered with black cloths.
A cellar with a steel door. The door has no handle, only a hole in the middle that leads inward.
A shaft that narrows downwards. At the narrowest point a shoe is stuck, its sole pointing upwards.
A tunnel that leads in two directions. At the fork lies a compass whose needle points to both ways at the same time.
A cellar with a pump. The pump is running, but the water in the collecting basin rises without any inlet being visible.
A shaft with a cable winch. The rope is taut, and from below one hears a weight striking against the wall.
A tunnel that ends in a room that is larger than the building above can be.

Shows what is hidden
Changes time by seconds
Answers a question
Stores power
Hits what cannot be hit
Measures what cannot be measured
Shows a place where one wants to be

1 strain per use

Watches nearby stop, forever
One page is afterwards written in the reader’s handwriting
It becomes warm and wants more
It wants to be used
It also measures the user, and someone is reading along
Whoever looks too long is there
Something is listening
The wearer is also concealed from friends
One does not know beforehand what
The former owner wants it back
A gas leak. The fire brigade ventilates, the municipal utilities seal it, the residents receive a letter.
An exercise by the Bundeswehr, police, and Technical Relief Service. The cordon was part of the scenario.
A smouldering fire in an old cable duct. The smells, lights, and noises come from burning insulation.
A film crew that shot for a series. Residents are asked not to publish photos.
A private security service that reported a break-in at a vacant building.
An error in the drinking water analysis. The authority recommends boiling the water until the values are correct.
A group of sleepwalkers affected by a medication trial. The clinic covers the costs.
A faulty transformer that caused power cuts and flickering. The energy supplier regrets the disruption.
An illegal rave in an old hall. The police confiscated the equipment and are investigating persons unknown.
A swarm of bats that got lost in a building. An expert relocated the animals.
A burst water pipe under the road. The construction site remains for two weeks, the diversion is signposted.
An elaborate prank by students. The police identified and cautioned those responsible.

tabellen.k: Weather / What it does to the scene
z: **Dense fog**: Sounds seem closer than they are. Every Perception test is one step harder.
**Heavy rain**: Traces are washed away, but conversations are hard to overhear. Stealth receives +1 die.
**Thunderstorm**: Lightning illuminates the place for seconds. Anyone moving outdoors must make a Concentration test against Easy (1) after each thunderclap.
**Snowfall**: The world becomes quiet. Footsteps leave clear traces, but sounds are muffled.
**Heat**: The air shimmers. Anyone carrying heavy equipment receives −1 die on physical tests after one hour.
**Cold**: Fingers become stiff. Sleight of Hand tests are one step harder as long as the hands are unprotected.
**Storm**: Loose objects fly about. Anyone who wants to hear something rolls Perception against Hard (3).
**Drizzle**: Everything is damp, nothing gets dry. Electronics fail on a botch.
**Clear night**: The moon shines. Visibility is good, but shadows are hard. Stealth outdoors is one step harder.
**Humidity**: The air is still. Smells linger. Anyone searching for a trace by smell receives +1 die.
**Hail**: Short and loud. Anyone outdoors seeks cover. Afterwards everything is covered with ice that makes noise.
**Calm**: Nothing moves. Every sound feels like a blow. Anyone listening receives +1 die on Perception.

tabellen.q: Random Files, What a Telepath Picks Up
z: A humming that does not come from the ears. It sounds like a choir waiting for its cue
A child singing in their sleep. The words are in no language the Psion knows
Cold that comes from within, and the smell of wet stone. Something has waited here
An image: a door that stands open, and behind it is not a room but a field of grey light
The taste of copper and the feeling that someone whispers the Telepath’s name without moving their lips
A memory that is not their own: a station, a train, a face reflected in the window that does not travel along
The feeling of being watched by something that has no eyes. It thinks in patterns, not in words
A sentence that repeats: “She said we shouldn’t open.” The voice belongs to an old woman
A pain that is not physical, as if their own skin were too tight. Something transformed and regrets it
Silence that is louder than any noise. Nothing thinks in this place, and that is unnatural
An image: a circle of salt on a wooden floor, and in the middle stands a chair that slowly turns
The feeling that time runs wrong, as if their own memory needed a moment longer than the world

tabellen.n: What Else Is in the Bag
tabellen.k: What You Always Have with You
tabellen.q: Class Book Psion, What Else Is in the Bag
z: A cloth handkerchief. For the nosebleeds
A bar of chocolate. Powers make you hungry
An old cassette with a song that calms you
A talisman from the time before your manifestation
A pair of earplugs too many, for someone who will need them
A note with a telephone number you never call

tabellen.n: What Else Is in the Bag
tabellen.k: What You Always Have with You
tabellen.q: Class Book Thaumaturge, What Else Is in the Bag
z: A piece of chalk, too short to write with, but too important to throw away
An empty lead box, in case you find something on the way
A pencil stub and a notebook for what the stone says at night
A candle, a box of matches, and a thread of silver
A slip of paper with the number of the first crystal you ever had
Peppermint against the taste of metal after a major spell

tabellen.q: Game Master's Book, What Happens During Downtime
z: A contact gets in touch. They need help, tonight.
The pay does not arrive. The front company has been shut down, a new one is being set up. Two weeks without money.
Someone from their private life has seen something they should not understand: a scar, a helmet, a passport.
The Audit requests a conversation. It is about another agent. Or allegedly.
An organisation makes an offer, from the table “The Lures of the Others”.
Quiet. Real quiet. The character may choose a third action.

tabellen.k: Furnishings / What the cell finds in the room
tabellen.q: Random Files, What Is in the Room
z: **A narrow bed, a chair, a table**: On the table stands a cup in which a dark liquid moves, although no one has entered the room.
**A desk with three drawers**: In the top drawer lies a bundle of old tickets, all for the same route, each cancelled on a different day.
**A shelf with empty folders**: On the floor in front of the shelf lies a single sheet on which only one name is written: that of a member of the cell.
**A workbench with tools**: On the wall hangs a board on which every tool is outlined in chalk, but one outline is empty and the tool lies beside it.
**A fridge that is still running**: In the fridge stand twelve glasses of water, all but one frozen.
**A wardrobe with an empty rail**: On the floor of the wardrobe lies a shoe that is warm inside.
**A sofa, a coffee table, a television**: The television is unplugged, but on the screen flickers a still image showing the room from one corner.
**A child’s room with a loft bed**: Under the mattress lies a notebook in which every page is filled with the same drawing: a circle with thirteen lines.
**A bathroom with a steamed-up mirror**: Someone has written a word on the mirror with a finger. It only becomes visible when the mirror steams up again.
**A kitchen with a long table**: On the table stands a plate of food that is still steaming, but the chair in front of it has been empty for days.
**A storage room with crates**: One crate is secured with a padlock that has no keyhole.
**An office with a filing cabinet**: In the wastepaper basket lies a torn letter that ends with “If you are reading this, I am already”.
**A hallway with a coat rack**: On the coat rack hangs a coat from whose pocket sand trickles that smells of ozone.
**A bedroom with a double bed**: On the pillow lies an imprint as if someone had lain there, but the duvet is pulled tight.
**A basement room with shelves**: Behind one shelf a narrow door leads into a room that is not marked on any plan.
**An attic with old furniture**: Under a sheet stands a packed suitcase with clothes from the fifties, freshly ironed and still warm from the iron.
**A garage with tools and tyres**: On the wall hangs a calendar on which a date in the future is circled in red, with the note “do not open”.
**A conference room with a blackboard**: On the blackboard is an equation that someone has half wiped away, but the rest gives the coordinates of a place nearby.
**A living room with a fireplace**: In the fireplace lies cold ash, but on top a piece of paper that is not burned.
**A study with a computer**: The computer is off, but the screen is warm, and on the keyboard sticks a note with a password.
**A dining room with a set table**: On a plate lies a photo showing the cell entering the building, from above.
**A stairwell with a landing**: On the landing stands a plant that has grown towards the wall, as if it had found light there.
**A boiler room with pipes**: One of the pipes is wrapped with a strip of cloth, under which a crystal shard has grown into the metal.
**A hobby room with a model railway**: The model railway shows the place where the building stands, but with an additional house that does not exist.
**An archive with index cards**: One index card is pulled out and lies crossways, as if someone had interrupted the search.
**A treatment room with an examination couch**: On the couch lies an instrument that does not belong in a treatment room and is still damp.
**A changing room with lockers**: One locker is open, and inside hangs a coverall with a badge that O.D.I.N. used before 1989.
**A waiting room with chairs**: On one chair lies a magazine reporting on an event that will only happen in two weeks.
**A server room with air conditioning**: The air conditioning is running, but the room is warm, and from a cabinet blinks a light that is not connected to the system.
**A meeting room with a map**: On the map a pin is stuck in a place where the cell has never been, but whose name appears in an open case.
**A lift with a cabin**: The lift moves although no one has called it, and stops on a floor that does not exist.
**A stair landing with a window**: The window shows a street that does not match the street where the building stands.
**A basement corridor with doors**: One door is marked with chalk, as if someone had counted, but the number is smudged.
**A washroom with basins**: From a tap drips a liquid that does not mix with the water in the basin.
**A storage room with filing cabinets**: One filing cabinet is empty, but the drawer is warm, and on the inside sticks a hair.
**An empty room with a light bulb**: The light bulb swings although there is no draught, and its shadow on the floor shows a second person.

tabellen.q: Random Files, What Is Really Behind It
z: The missing person has not vanished, they are shifted: eight minutes into the future.
The victim was not a victim. They opened the rift themselves, with a ritual from a book they thought was a novel.
The witness is not lying. They remember two different evenings, and both are true.
The crystal was not stolen. It has gone, and someone opened the Door for it.
The children saw nothing. They only sang what the dead woman had sung to them.
The perpetrator has been dead for three days. What the cell hunts wears him.
Morrow Biologics did not cause the incident, but calculated it in advance and did nothing.
STILLWATER knew about the rift before it opened. Its sensors were there first.
An Open One touched the crystal. They only wanted to see whether O.D.I.N. really takes everything.
The Foundation in Basel once possessed the object. Its file on it ends with a name from the cell.
Grey Meridian did not receive the contract, but declined it, and that is more disturbing.
An Enlightened One advised the collector. The collect- or believes to this day it was their own idea.
The house is not cursed. It stands on a plot that belonged to another organisation in 1938.
The dead man did not come through the rift. He was always here, only deeper.
The device was not built. It grew, and at night.
The missing woman wanted to be found. She laid the trail herself, but not for O.D.I.N.
The rift is not new. It was closed in 1971, and someone has opened it again.
The creature did not hunt. It fed, and the cell is the food.
The handler knows the place. They were there twenty years ago, under a different name.
The file in the archive is redacted because the Council wanted to protect the victim’s name. From the cell.
The artefact does not act on the cell because it is waiting for one of them.
The cult has no leader. The voice it follows comes from a crystal in the wall.
The police covered nothing up. They never saw the case because someone rewrote their files.
The witness is a former Cadet who dropped out of training. They recognise the cell’s methods.
The corpse in the bog is not the first. It is the first that was meant to be found.
The rift has no opening. It is a seam, and the cell is standing directly on it.
The child has no psionics. They have carried a shard under their skin for as long as they can remember.
The collector never possessed the crystal. They only own the receipt, and it is genuine.
The animals did not flee. They gathered, just not where the cell searched.
The call did not come from outside. It came from the archive, from a room that has been locked for years.
The organisation that caused the incident no longer exists. Its debts, however, do.
The dead man knew O.D.I.N. In his pocket is an old service ID with the face of a Council member.
The weather was not a coincidence. Someone ordered it, with a ritual that trades rain for silence.
The trail leads to the cell itself. One of them was at the same place years ago without knowing it.
The rift is closed. What is still there now does not want to go back.
The truth is banal: a person lied out of fear, and everything else grew from that lie.

tabellen.n: What Is Wrong with the Building
tabellen.q: Random Files, What Is Wrong with the Building
z: All doors in the building are open a crack, but no light is on anywhere.
A smell of wet stone hangs in the stairwell, although it has not rained for weeks.
The floors are slightly sloped, just enough that a ball rolls into a corner by itself.
Finger-wide strips of black tape stick to all mirrors, as if someone had wanted to hide something.
The house has more windows from outside than rooms inside. One of them is nowhere to be found from inside.
The letterbox contains post addressed to no one who has ever lived here, but all envelopes bear the name of an agent.
The walls are warm in one place, cold in another, and the boundary between them runs exactly vertically.
All clocks in the building have stopped, each at a different time, and together the times form a code.
A calendar hangs in the cellar, on which every day until the end of the year is crossed out, except today’s.
The building casts a shadow that does not match its shape, as if something else stood beside it that no one sees.
The front door is secured from inside with three locks, two bolts and a chain, but all keys are in the locks from outside.
From a room that should not exist, one hears a steady knocking that stops exactly when someone stands before it.

tabellen.q: Random Files, What Remains After a File
z: A witness saw more than he admits. He does not come forward, but he watches the cell from now on.
A local reporter requested access to the file. The Print Shop considers him harmless, but he keeps writing.
A skull of an opponent’s plan fills. The organisation has learned from the incident.
A name on a list remains unexplained. It belongs to no one the cell knows, but it appears in other files.
An item from the operation was not turned in. It lies in a bag, in a locker, under a bed.
A resident made a video. It is blurry, but someone shared it in a forum.
A contact of the cell has questions. They do not ask them, but they note who could answer them.
A handler asks for an addendum to the report. They ask about a detail the cell omitted.
A place remains closed. The cordon is official, but the reason has been changed.
A member of the cell dreams about the operation. The dream repeats until something is done.
A call comes in, but no one speaks. The number belongs to a line that does not exist.
A file is upgraded one level. The cell only learns of it when they receive the next one.

tabellen.n: What Stands Out at the Crime Scene
tabellen.q: Random Files, What Stands Out at the Crime Scene
z: **A half footprint in the dust under a window**: Tracking against Doable (2)
**A hair on the door handle that does not come from the victim**: Biology against Hard (3)
**A scratch on the lock that comes from the inside**: Security Systems against Doable (2)
**A piece of fabric on a nail that smells of ozone**: Perception against Easy (1)
**A handprint on the wall that is larger than any hand in the room**: Investigation against Hard (3)
**A puddle that does not dry although the room is warm**: Chemistry against Doable (2)
**A tipped-over chair that has remained standing on one leg**: Physics against Easy (1)
**A notebook with a missing page**: Investigation against Doable (2)
**A telephone that is still dialling although no one answers**: Technology against Hard (3)
**A mirror that shows the room but without the corpse**: Perception against Hard (3)
**A piece of chalk on the floor that belongs to a circle**: Occultism against Doable (2)
**A window that is fogged up from the outside**: Tracking against Doable (2)
**A drop of blood that runs upward**: Physics against Hard (3)
**An ashtray with a still smouldering cigarette whose smoke sinks downward**: Perception against Easy (1)
**A photo that shows the crime scene before the victim died**: Investigation against Hard (3)
**A smell of burnt hair coming from the wall**: Chemistry against Doable (2)
**A key that fits no lock in the building**: Security Systems against Hard (3)
**An impression in the carpet as if something heavy had stood there for a long time**: Tracking against Easy (1)
**A letter written in handwriting that does not belong to the victim**: Investigation against Doable (2)
**A radio that plays quietly although it is unplugged**: Technology against Hard (3)
**A shoe that is clean although the floor is covered in blood**: Tracking against Hard (3)
**A calendar on which a day that has not yet happened is crossed out**: Perception against Easy (1)
**A thread stretched from the door to the window**: Perception against Hard (3)
**A glass that is still fogged up although the room has been empty for hours**: Chemistry against Doable (2)
**A book lying open on the floor; the lines of the open page change as soon as no one is looking**: Occultism against Doable (2)
**A piece of metal that feels cold although it lay in the sun**: Physics against Hard (3)
**An imprint of a bare foot that ends in the wall**: Tracking against Hard (3)
**A note with a sequence of numbers that matches no known code**: Cryptography against Hard (3)
**A stain on the ceiling that looks like a face**: Perception against Easy (1)
**A chair that moves when one enters the room although no one is sitting on it**: Mental Resistance against Doable (2)
**A mobile phone showing a video that the dead person cannot have recorded**: Technology against Hard (3)
**A remnant of black candle wax into which someone has pressed a symbol**: Occultism against Doable (2)
**A key ring that is still warm and missing one key**: Perception against Easy (1)
**A stack of receipts, all from the same shop, all with the same time**: Investigation against Hard (3)
**A piece of paper that unfolds by itself when touched**: Occultism against Hard (3)
**A shadow that remains when one turns on the light**: Mental Resistance against Hard (3)

tabellen.q: Random Files, What the Dead Man Carried
z: A key without a bit, worn on a chain around the neck, and the chain has grown into the skin.
A wallet with a photograph of a woman, labelled on the back with a name that appears in none of the dead man’s documents.
A crumpled note with an address that leads to a house demolished ten years ago.
A mobile phone that, when opened, shows a single message: “Stay in the light.” Sent at 3:14 a.m.
A small stuffed animal, cut open at the belly and sewn shut again, with a crystal shard stuck inside it.
A pocket knife whose blade is coated with a dark layer that cannot be wiped off.
A notebook in which every page begins with the same sentence: “I am not alone.”
An envelope with cash, the notes all having the same serial number ending and smelling of damp earth.
A compass whose glass is cracked and whose needle stubbornly points downward, as if north lay deep underground.
An identity card listing the dead man as an employee of a company that has not existed for fifteen years.
A small glass tube sealed with a cork, containing a liquid that pulses faintly in the dark.
A note with a sequence of numbers that seems familiar to the cell because it appears in an open file of the organisation.

tabellen.q: Random Files, What the Instruments Show
z: **The EMF meter spikes although no power line is nearby**: A presence that disturbs electromagnetic fields. Origin the Dead or the Machine
**The Geiger counter shows a value above background, but the isotope is unknown**: Something from the Shifted has been here. The radiation decays too slowly
**The thermal camera shows a cold spot in a warm room that moves**: An entity that draws heat. Origin the Dead or the Old
